# Editing routes

| Route | Starting point |
| --- | --- |
| Resolve | `edit-in-resolve` (follows the edition's workflow); Studio: `resolve recipe assemble`; Free: `resolve free-import`, then `resolve free-edit` |
| FFmpeg | [Assembly](../../make-ai-video/references/assembly.md); bundled `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` |
| AE | `capture prepare-ae`, then `edit-in-after-effects` |

Automatic capture-recipe conversion currently targets AE. Resolve/FFmpeg need
an adapted script/filter graph, especially for cursor telemetry, zoom and
person mattes. The simple `media assemble` recipe handles trims, text/logo
overlays and audio timing; it does not interpret capture recipes.

## Timing for adapted scripts

- Use each track's `startUs`/`durationUs` from `capture.json`
  to place media on the capture clock; tracks need not start together.
- Share ordered cuts, speeds and repeats across screen, camera, cursor and audio.
  Segments are half-open; a boundary event belongs to the following segment.
- Speech outputs share one plan/render timeline. Apply it to picture, use the
  already-edited WAV without retiming it again, replace its original dialogue
  layer, and use output-timed captions and `facecamHide` spans.
- Cursor events use capture-clock `timeUs`; mapping needs geometry, pixel scale,
  hotspots and visibility. Share screen crop/zoom with the cursor. `system`
  mode bakes the pointer into video; `editable` mode needs a telemetry adapter.
- Matte `frames.ndjson` times are camera-media times: add `sourceStartUs` before
  applying edits. Hold each PNG to the next measured timestamp (last to camera
  end), with identical camera/matte crop and mirror. Numbering is not a frame clock.
- Zoom/facecam animation defaults to output time; `animationTime: "source"`
  requests retiming through cuts and repeats.

A floating-head area is a **facecam/PiP overlay**; its shape an **aperture
mask**; room removal a **person matte**. Keep these controls separate. Use
geometric masks for circles, segmentation for transparent cutouts or
background changes.

For editor choices and camera/matte timing, see
[editing routes](editing-routes.md). The recipe below
has an automatic AE adapter; Resolve/FFmpeg use adapted scripts.

## Optional capture recipe

For a Voyager capture bundle, add a `facecam` object to the composition recipe, for example:

```json
{
  "width": 320,
  "height": 320,
  "position": [1690, 850],
  "focalPoint": [0.5, 0.45],
  "mirror": true,
  "mask": { "kind": "circle" },
  "border": { "width": 6, "color": [1, 1, 1] },
  "shadow": { "offset": [0, 12], "opacity": 35, "blur": 20, "color": [0, 0, 0] }
}
```

Dimensions/position are composition pixels; position is the aperture center.
Options include `rounded-rectangle` with a pixel `radius`; a custom closed
`path` with matching vertices/inTangents/outTangents; or PNG
`mask: {kind:"image",path:"mask.png",channel:"alpha"}` (`luma` is also available).
PNG `foreground` adds custom frame artwork. Optional label, border, shadow,
focal point and motion remain editable. Paths are relative to the recipe.

## Optional background removal

```sh
voyager capture matte ./captures/demo --output ./demo-matte --request-id demo_matte_1 --json
voyager capture matte-status matte_RETURNED_ID --json
```

The Mac helper uses Apple Vision offline. `matte-doctor --json` checks runtime
support; `matte-cancel ID --json` cancels a queued/active job. `--quality` accepts
fast/balanced/accurate. Optional `--feather` softens edges; `--temporal-weight`
blends adjacent masks and can cause trails. Defaults leave both disabled.
Exact retries return the same job; poll an uncertain result before submitting
another job.

Once complete, add `"matte":"./demo-matte"` to `facecam`. Without a background,
the person is transparent over the recording. Choose one of `background` PNG,
`backgroundColor` RGB or `backgroundBlur` radius; blur requires a person matte.
Optional `outline: {width:3,color:[1,1,1]}` outlines the person independently of
the aperture border. Matte PNGs have measured timestamps, not an assumed frame
rate; the prepared AE import shares camera timing, crop and mirror.

`capture prepare-ae BUNDLE --recipe edit.json --output NEW_DIR --json` creates
an import package for the existing AE tools. Review moving edges when segmentation matters;
a still frame alone cannot reveal flicker or motion trails.

# Demo Mac recording

The VM has separate apps, accounts, files and permissions from the host.

Check `vm.doctor` first. Demo Mac is opt-in under Settings → Labs → Demo Mac;
`enabled: false` means this recording route is unavailable. Do not enable it on
the user's behalf. When enabled and the destination is unspecified, ask whether
to record on the host or in a disposable demo Mac before creating a VM or starting
capture. An explicit destination or earlier choice does not need reconfirmation.

Use `media_describe` with `vm` to discover schemas. In Voyager, `vm_command`
executes these commands and returns observation images. The external Voyager MCP
uses `media_command`; the shared CLI exposes `voyager vm <operation> --json`.
All calls in a task need the same workspace and external session identity:

```sh
export VOYAGER_EXTERNAL_SESSION_ID="product-demo-task"
voyager vm doctor --json
```

Prepare a base with `vm.prepare` only when needed, then poll `vm.prepare-status`.
The user completes macOS setup, automatic login, the guest installer, and guest
Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions in the displayed VM. `vm.seal`
verifies the agent and saves the base. Do not put product logins into the base.
`vm.create` clones it; `vm.start` boots the returned ID. Poll `vm.status` until
`ready: true`; booted does not mean permissions and guest connection are ready.

Use `vm.open-url` for a public product URL. For a local development server,
`vm.forward` exposes exactly its host loopback port and returns a guest URL.
Guest localhost refers to the guest. Project sharing is off by default; request
`mountProject: "read-only"` or `"read-write"` on creation only when needed.
Use `vm.launch` for apps already installed in the guest; `vm.exec` runs inside
that guest, never on the physical host.

Rehearse the important visible action and outcome before recording. Use
`vm.observe`, inspect the returned screenshot, then act with its `observation`
token. Coordinates are pixels in the 1920×1080 observation. Tokens expire and are
consumed by input; observe again after each action. The guest cursor is
visible in recorded footage. `vm.wait` provides bounded pacing.

Start a take with `vm.record-start` and a stable request ID. Do the walkthrough
using short observe/action/verify steps; end on the product result long enough
for a viewer to understand it. Recording is silent and guest-only. Keep setup,
authentication, and unrelated dialogs out of the take.

Stop input on human takeover.
Resume only after the user returns control, and obtain a new observation.
Pausing input does not stop a recording. In standalone shell workflows, renew the
external session with `voyager computer heartbeat` during long gaps.

Use `vm.record-stop` to finalize and export the take. Return its project path.

Stop or delete the disposable VM after delivery unless the user wants to keep it.
Reset restores guest state only; it
does not undo host-mounted file writes or online service actions. A VM failure is
never permission to switch to host computer control or host recording.

---
name: screen-capture
description: "Record screen, window, camera and audio with editable cursor telemetry; style presenter camera tracks."
applications:
  - id: after-effects
    role: alternative
  - id: resolve
    role: alternative
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: fallback
  - id: photoshop
    role: alternative
---

`voyager capture` records only on macOS, through the signed Voyager desktop
companion on that Mac. On Windows and Linux every recording command returns
`UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`: tell the user, and ask for their own screen recordings.
Existing bundles can still be inspected and prepared there.

Save recordings to the requested location, or a new project-local
`captures/<name>-<timestamp>/` directory. Create its parent if needed; capture
creates the take directory. Process only when requested.

[Editing routes](references/editing-routes.md) covers Resolve, FFmpeg and optional
AE, with timing and adapter details.
For presenter/facecam styling (floating heads, PiP, apertures, background
removal), read [facecam styling](references/facecam.md).
If their own footage has someone talking, [edit by text](../edit-video/SKILL.md) is available.

## Recording

`capture doctor --json` runs from any directory and never requests a permission. Read
`capabilities`: one resolved verdict per capability (`screen`, `window`, `region`,
`systemAudio`, `camera`, `microphone`, `editableCursor`, ...) that folds build
support, permission and what ScreenCaptureKit enumerated into `{ ready, reason }`.
`reason` names the remedy: `PERMISSION_REQUIRED` means run `capture setup`,
`CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE` means a stale screen grant (window capture may still be
ready), and `UNSUPPORTED` means this build cannot do it. `capture sources
--json` lists display/window IDs and also returns `ready`, with `reason` and
`message` when it is false. A false verdict means displays and system audio
cannot be captured on this machine right now — window IDs are still listed and
still record, so prefer a window source rather than reporting failure. `capture
devices --json` lists camera/mic IDs. Reuse known valid IDs; do not substitute a different device. For a missing
permission, `capture setup --permission screen|camera|microphone|cursor --json`
requests that permission or opens its system settings. It may show an OS prompt.

Window sources include offscreen windows reported by macOS, with `isOnScreen`
indicating current visibility. A missing thumbnail does not mean a window is
unavailable. Before filming visible interaction, open/activate the intended app, restore a minimized window using computer
control if needed, and refresh sources. Reuse the exact window ID while it exists;
never substitute another window or a display silently. Offscreen/minimized apps
may stop updating their content, so verify a short recording after bringing the
window onscreen. If macOS omits the window entirely, activate the app and refresh
before reporting it unavailable. Granted screen permission does not need another
setup request.

For shell calls outside Voyager, reuse a task-specific external session for start,
status, stop and previews. The MCP adapter supplies its own session and heartbeats
automatically. Shell calls must keep the lease alive: poll capture status within
90 seconds or run a bounded heartbeat alongside longer recordings. Heartbeat
expiry or cancellation closes that session and stops its recording, so choose
its duration to cover the take and explicitly stop the take when done.

```sh
export VOYAGER_EXTERNAL_SESSION_ID="demo-task-unique-id"
voyager capture start --source display:ID --camera CAMERA_ID --microphone MIC_ID \
  --system-audio --cursor editable --fps 30 --output ./captures/demo \
  --request-id demo_take_1 --json
# Optional for long takes: run alongside recording; closes the session after 5 minutes.
voyager computer heartbeat --duration 300 --json &
voyager capture status cap_RETURNED_ID --json
voyager capture stop cap_RETURNED_ID --json
voyager capture inspect ./captures/demo --json
```

Remove unused source flags; camera-only and audio-only recordings are supported.
`--system-audio` records the system output mix, including other apps and Voyager
playback, even when video is limited to one window. It does not record the mic.
Verify sound with a short take while a known audible sample is actually playing;
a present audio track alone does not prove it contains sound.
A display can use `--region '{"x":100,"y":100,"width":1280,"height":720}'` in
logical display points. Cursor modes are `editable` (separate events/artwork,
extra OS permission), `system` (baked into footage) and `hidden` (default).
Output is a new directory inside the active workspace (`voyager --workspace /path capture ...`). All requested tracks must
start; a partial start is an error. The tray also provides Stop.

Reuse the same request ID for an exact retry and collect its receipt after a
timeout. Changed inputs need a new ID. An uncertain recording never resumes or
replays itself. Keep the original bundle intact: `capture.json`, separate media,
`events.ndjson` and cursor PNGs form one portable recording.

For product-demo requests, [make-product-demo](../make-product-demo/SKILL.md)
chooses the production route; not every demo needs recording.

## Agent-driven demos

When recording the agent operating an app, pair this skill with `use-computer`
only for UI-only steps or requested visible-pointer interaction. Prefer the app's
integration during the recording too: use `voyager resolve` for supported Resolve
operations, and the AE/Photoshop/browser integrations for their supported work.
Recording does not require replacing efficient integration calls with clicks.

For an edited product or launch demo, take direction from
[make-product-demo](../make-product-demo/SKILL.md) and read
[recorded demos](../use-computer/references/recorded-demos.md) for combining
recording with computer control. Keep recording and computer-control IDs and
authority separate.

## Optional AE preparation

`voyager capture prepare-ae --help` sketches the recipe: composition, shared
cuts/speeds, cursor, zoom and facecam. Times are integer microseconds. Optional
`animationTime: "source"` retimes zoom/facecam keys through the same cuts and
repeats; the default `"output"` lets you animate the finished edit directly.

```sh
voyager capture prepare-ae ./captures/demo --recipe ./edit.json --output ./demo-ae --json
```

Minimal recipe: `{"version":1,"composition":{"width":1920,"height":1080,"fps":30}}`.
For editable telemetry, add `"cursor":{"version":1,"smoothing":0.65,"size":1.2,
"theme":"captured","clickEffect":"ring"}`. `theme: "arrow"` uses a vector cursor.
Clicks anchor the path; raw telemetry remains available for other editors.

Preparation writes `import.jsx` and `parameters.json`; it does not launch AE.
With AE selected, the bundled `edit-in-after-effects` skill covers execution:
`voyager ae execute --project /absolute/demo.aep --file ./demo-ae/import.jsx
--input @./demo-ae/parameters.json --request-id ae_demo_1 --json` (one shell line).
It adds editable layers/compositions without switching or saving the project.
Preparation references absolute source paths; regenerate after moving a bundle.
Use [facecam styling](references/facecam.md) or [speech edits](../edit-video/references/speech-edits.md) when those edits are relevant.

### Native cursor visibility limit

The current Mac helper reports `cursorVisibility` as unsupported (doctor:
`{ "ready": false, "reason": "UNSUPPORTED" }`; bundle manifest: `false`). It preserves pointer
positions and infers visibility outside the capture bounds, but cannot detect a
foreground app hiding its cursor globally. Choose `--cursor system` when native
hide/reveal behavior matters more than replacement.
